searched: Retrieved 2026-10-27, sequentially. TC260: tc260.org.cn news list pages 1-12, notices, publications (出版物) and the news items for versions 1.0 (2024-09-10) and 3.0 (2026-09-14); the v1.0 PDF URL cited in later documents (tc260.org.cn/upload/2024-09-09/1725849192841090989.pdf) now redirects to TC260's home page, so the Chinese v1.0 PDF and the bilingual v2.0 PDF were taken from cac.gov.cn, where the CAC news items link them; no v2.0 item was found on tc260.org.cn. A version 3.0 (September 2026) was found and is included. AIIA: aiiaorg.cn (home page only; no commitment page), aihub.caict.ac.cn (working-group page is a JavaScript shell; the commitments disclosure page cited in CAICT's January 2026 blue book returns 404), caict.ac.cn news list via relay, and CAICT's WeChat posts of 23 and 24 December 2024; the 24 December post carries the commitment text and initial signatory list only as an embedded image, read visually. Text reproductions: itcloudbd.com (matches the image), People's Daily Online (differs in commitment two), Guangzhou Daily (dayoo.com; gives the date as 11月24日, apparently an error) and People's Daily Online of 18 July 2025 (22 signatories reported; no list). Sina Finance refused (HTTP 403). Carnegie Endowment's January 2025 analysis and an AI Safety in China newsletter were used for discovery only. The 2025 中国人工智能安全承诺框架 (WAIC, July 2025) and the later signatories were not retrieved. Shanghai AI Laboratory's Frontier AI Risk Management Framework v1.0: English PDF from concordia-ai.com; no copy on a Shanghai AI Laboratory domain was found; it cites TC260's framework but no commitment. Searches for frontier safety frameworks published by Zhipu, MiniMax or 01.AI under the Seoul commitments found none; METR's tracker could not be retrieved. web.archive.org was not used.

claims.subject: tc260
claims.statement: TC260 (全国网络安全标准化技术委员会) released version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework on 9 September 2024 at the main forum of the 2024 National Cybersecurity Awareness Week.

time.note: Release date stated in TC260's news item (page dated 2024-09-10); the PDF cover gives 2024年9月.

claims.qualification: Records the release as TC260 states it. The framework calls itself a framework of technical and governance measures; this record does not establish legal force, adoption or implementation by anyone.

evidence.passage: 9月9日，在2024年国家网络安全宣传周主论坛上，全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 ... 发布《人工智能安全治理框架》1.0版

translation.text: On 9 September, at the main forum of the 2024 National Cybersecurity Awareness Week, the National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee ... released version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework

evidence.passage: 全国网络安全标准化技术委员会 2024年9月

translation.text: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee, September 2024

claims.subject: tc260-asgf-v1-0

object.value: Registration and filing of AI systems above compute or reasoning thresholds or in specific sectors

claims.statement: Version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework proposes registration and filing for AI systems whose computing power or reasoning capability reaches certain thresholds, or which are applied in specific sectors.

time.note: Release date of the cited edition; the provision's own effect or application date is not stated.

claims.qualification: What version 1.0 says, among comprehensive governance measures. The thresholds are not quantified in the text; no registration system is shown to exist by this record.

evidence.locator: §5.1 实施人工智能应用分类分级管理
evidence.passage: 对算力、推理能力达到一定阈值或应用在特定行业领域的人工智能系统进行登记备案

translation.text: carry out registration and filing for AI systems whose computing power or reasoning capability reaches a certain threshold or that are applied in specific industry sectors

claims.subject: tc260-asgf-v1-0

object.value: Classification and grading of AI systems with a risk-level testing and evaluation system

claims.statement: Version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework proposes classifying and grading AI systems and establishing a risk-level testing and evaluation system.

time.note: Release date of the cited edition; the provision's own effect or application date is not stated.

claims.qualification: What the cited edition says. It is not evidence that any measure was adopted, implemented or enforced, or that any developer falls within it.

evidence.locator: §5.1 实施人工智能应用分类分级管理
evidence.passage: 对人工智能系统分类分级,建立风险等级测试评估体系

translation.text: classify and grade AI systems and establish a testing and evaluation system for risk levels

claims.subject: tc260-asgf-v1-0

object.value: Screen training data to exclude sensitive data in high-risk fields such as nuclear, biological, chemical and missile weapons

claims.statement: Version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework lists, as a technical countermeasure, strict screening of training data to ensure it contains no sensitive data from high-risk fields such as nuclear, biological, chemical and missile weapons.

time.note: Release date of the cited edition; the provision's own effect or application date is not stated.

claims.qualification: What version 1.0 says. 核生化导 is rendered as nuclear, biological, chemical and missile; the text does not say who verifies the screening.

evidence.passage: 对训练数据进行严格筛选,确保不包含核生化导武器等高危领域敏感数据

translation.text: strictly screen training data to ensure it does not contain sensitive data in high-risk fields such as nuclear, biological, chemical and missile weapons

claims.subject: tc260-asgf-v1-0

object.value: Improve end-use traceability to prevent use in manufacturing weapons of mass destruction

claims.statement: Version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework lists improving the traceability of AI systems' end use, to prevent their use in high-risk scenarios such as manufacturing nuclear, biological, chemical or missile weapons of mass destruction.

time.note: Release date of the cited edition; the provision's own effect or application date is not stated.

claims.qualification: What the cited edition says. It is not evidence that any measure was adopted, implemented or enforced, or that any developer falls within it.

evidence.passage: 提高人工智能系统最终用途追溯能力,防止被用于核生化导等大规模杀伤性武器制造等高危场景

translation.text: improve the ability to trace the end use of AI systems, to prevent them being used in high-risk scenarios such as manufacturing nuclear, biological, chemical, missile and other weapons of mass destruction

claims.subject: tc260-asgf-v1-0

object.value: Industry associations to draw up AI safety self-discipline conventions above regulatory requirements

claims.statement: Version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework proposes guiding and supporting industry associations in cybersecurity and AI to draw up AI safety self-discipline conventions that go beyond regulatory requirements.

time.note: Release date of the cited edition; the provision's own effect or application date is not stated.

claims.qualification: What version 1.0 says. This record does not connect the provision to any later industry commitment; no such link is stated in the framework or in the commitment texts inspected for this pack.

evidence.passage: 行业协会加强行业自律,制定提出高于监管要求、具有引领示范作用的人工智能安全自律公约

translation.text: industry associations strengthen industry self-discipline and draw up AI safety self-discipline conventions that are higher than regulatory requirements and serve as leading examples

claims.subject: tc260

claims.subject: shanghai-ai-lab
claims.statement: Shanghai AI Laboratory, in collaboration with Concordia AI, introduced the Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0), dated July 2025 in its own citation line.

time.note: Month in the document's own citation line; no day is stated.

claims.qualification: The framework presents itself as a guideline for general-purpose AI model developers. It is not recorded as a commitment by Shanghai AI Laboratory about its own models, and this record does not establish adoption by any developer.

evidence.passage: Today, Shanghai AI Laboratory, in collaboration with Concordia AI
How to cite this report: Shanghai AI Lab and Concordia AI, “Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0),” July 2025.
This framework serves as a guideline for general-purpose AI model developers to manage the potential severe risks from their general-purpose AI models.

claims.statement: Concordia AI is named with Shanghai AI Laboratory in the citation line of the Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0), July 2025.

time.note: Month in the document's own citation line; no day is stated.

claims.subject: sail-frontier-ai-risk-management-framework-v1-0
claims.statement: The Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0) states that it builds upon the International AI Safety Report (January 2025) and TC260's AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0, which it cites in a footnote.

time.note: Month of the citing document.

claims.qualification: An explicit citation with the words 'builds upon'. It does not establish what was taken from the cited framework, endorsement by TC260, or any institutional relation.

evidence.passage: Our Framework builds upon the International AI Safety Report (January 2025) ... and AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0
National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity of SAC, "AI Safety Governance Framework," 2024

claims.subject: sail-frontier-ai-risk-management-framework-v1-0

object.value: Red lines as intolerable thresholds and yellow lines as early-warning indicators

claims.statement: The Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0) defines red lines as intolerable thresholds that must not be crossed and yellow lines as early-warning indicators for potential risks.

time.note: Month of the cited edition.

claims.qualification: What the framework says. It proposes thresholds for cyber offense, biological threats, large-scale persuasion and manipulation, and loss of control; whether any developer adopted them is not recorded.

evidence.locator: §2.1 Defining “Yellow Lines” and “Red Lines” for AI Development
evidence.passage: defining “red lines” as intolerable thresholds that must not be crossed, and “yellow lines” as early warning indicators for potential risks

claims.subject: sail-frontier-ai-risk-management-framework-v1-0

object.value: Recommend suspending operations or deployment when red lines are crossed

claims.statement: The Frontier AI Risk Management Framework (v1.0) recommends that model developers, when red lines are crossed, suspend relevant operations or deployment until the risk is reduced below the red lines.

time.note: Month of the cited edition.

claims.qualification: A recommendation addressed to model developers, as worded ('we recommend'); not an undertaking by the publishers and not evidence of implementation.

evidence.passage: When red lines are crossed, we recommend that model developers to: ... Suspend relevant operations or deployment until the risk is reduced below red lines.
